series: Still Two People / 结婚以后，仍然是两个人 · 婚姻论
scope: A short guide and seven complete reader essays, not every proposition or historical/philosophical comparison. Complete Simplified and Traditional Chinese with independently written English.
method: Lead-authored Chinese and independent English; no translation service or subagents. Core distinctions and fictional cases checked against the overview, the forty-five propositions and corresponding papers. Added domestic details remain disclosed as fictional illustrations.
editorial_boundaries: The scope concerns one kind of marriage between two adults; it does not deny other forms, grade people, prescribe marriage or require children. Gender combination is not an entrance condition.

Love, each person's undertaking and institutional recognition are not interchangeable. Recording the operation of rules does not endorse their legitimacy. Recognition does not confer ownership of a spouse.
Daily re-affirmation does not mean daily expiry. Commitments bind through one's standing and effects already left in another life; change does not reset those effects to zero.

The two meanings of we do not create a third person entitled to settle individual judgment. A joint task needs both participants' assent. Regard is not total transparency, trust in every explanation or immunity from scrutiny.

Support offers conditions and questions, not a completed identity. Refusing exchange-debt does not erase contributions, property, labor, responsibilities or boundaries; no demand to endure unilateral self-erasure.

An arrangement can change without either person's underlying direction changing; private revision does not automatically create a new agreement. Expectations do not retroactively create obligations. Diagnosis attaches to a particular operation, not a person.

Old divisions of labor are neither automatically exchanges nor permanent identities. No sentence-form test. Quiet does not certify care, conflict is not prescribed, later agreement does not justify earlier harm.

Preparation concerns conditions for a newcomer, including adoption. Different reasons for joining can be genuine; no assent may be supplied by a partner. Revision, refusal and actual access remain distinct from erasing past effects.

Non-arrival does not undo preparation or establish personal/marital deficiency. A newcomer is not a product, an extension or a pre-agreed repayment source. Dependence does not transfer their standing or authorship of a life to adults.

After a child arrives, this series treats the couple's side of care, not a complete parent-child theory. Personal acts and contributions cannot be transferred to the other parent. Joint care does not end automatically on leaving marriage.

Love, promises, interaction and formal dissolution can end at different times. Love ending at one end changes the inquiry's scope, not the status or worth of the people, and does not prescribe their next life.

Obstacles, nonperformance, joint revision and inward deception are distinguished. An intelligible declaration is not an application for permission. No prescribed face-to-face farewell or unsafe contact is required.
Withdrawal and formal dissolution are distinct, not a universal legal procedure. A door's status cannot certify a person's inward affirmation. Existing responsibility is not a veto over departure.
Bereavement is not withdrawal; death does not certify the end of the survivor's love. No afterlife conclusion or grief timetable. Warmth neither erases harm nor guarantees reconciliation.
